newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes plentiful, demand still soft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes plentiful, demand still soft.

text.p: Foreign crudes offered into the U.S. Gulf Coast were plentiful Tuesday, reflecting the wide trans-Atlantic arbitrage, but refiner demand remained soft, traders said.
The spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent for February was around $1.70 a barrel, a level which allows sellers to make money moving cargoes across the Atlantic.
A number of Brent cargoes are on offer, ranging in price from WTI minus 25 cents for early February barrels to WTI minus 40-45 cents for late-February cargoes.

A number of West African crudes, such as Nigerian Qua Iboe, are also looking for a home on the Gulf Coast. One Bonny Light cargo for arrival February 1-10 was heard done at a price equivalent to Dated Brent plus 70 cents.
The day also featured unconfirmed reports of Russian Urals heading toward the United States.

Weak margins have undercut refiner demand, particularly on amid some major refinery turnarounds. Many refiners had delayed turnarounds in the fourth quarter to buoy heating oil stocks, and now are playing catch-up, analysts said.

Gulf Coast refiners operated by Exxon Corp, Citgo Petroleum Corp, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp and Clark Refining and Marketing set early January turnarounds to complete schedulaed maintenance on refining units, sources said.
Most Latin American crudes are also garnering tepid interest. Cusiana for late January is on offer at March WTI minus five cents, down from a recent discount of 10 cents.

Sour Ecuadoran Oriente, however, seems to be moving steadily, traders said. Key broker Tripetrol is sold out through February, and has March barrels on offer at April West Texas Sour minus $1.00 a barrel, they said.
In the U.S. aftermarket, two full boats of February Brent changed hands at $24.66/24.67 a barrel, eight to nine cents more than the IPE settlement.
Partials moved at $24.61/24.65 a barrel, three to seven cents over the London close.
